assessments.reasoning: The creativecommons.org legal-code response has lang="de", the Creative Commons masthead, a “Lizenzvertrag” heading and German contract text. Section 1(b) names all three elements displayed in the title. All three contiguous parts report the claimed publisher digest and cover the complete page.

The License Index’s own SCOPE.md at cdff8aeed68bf1f9c62d8c86159c7dc08b2d75d7, bytes [533,639), admits a license with identifiable text, edition and controlling source. The publisher’s 2.0 text and §3 licensing clause meet that criterion. The scope document assigns instrument authority to the publisher and editorial authority to the Index.

The Index’s 2026-11-26 decision at 8292fe4eef1269be7758d8c912d7f99a2aff6141, bytes [1935,2222), gives permanent entity 3dfd9fd542244acea1165b627aa4bd9b, matching subject e-3dfd9fd542244acea1165b627aa4bd9b. That row gives edition cc-by-nc-sa-2-0-de-publisher-reference, revision sha256:d88be489f05079a292baa8faf4bdf81153c2748198da6d4a654428993749cea4, kind license and state active. The revision matches the publisher receipt. The publisher’s older-version notice is consistent with continued Index maintenance.

I read §8(f) across publisher parts 2 and 3. At byte boundary 32768, “Deutschlan” continues with “d Anwendung.” The complete sentence reads “Auf diesen Lizenzvertrag findet das Recht der Bundesrepublik Deutschland Anwendung.” It supplies the claimed context independently of the title wording. Both publisher bindings use the same capture.

challenge.method: Compared the heading, identifier and §1(b) elements with all six 3.0 Deutschland rows in the Index decision, including the closest BY-NC-SA row. Checked §4(b)’s Japan example, the older-version notice, the footer and the separate governing-law passage for competing readings.
challenge.results: The BY, BY-NC, BY-NC-ND, BY-NC-SA, BY-ND and BY-SA 3.0 reference titles each end in “3.0 Deutschland”. Even the closest row uses “Keine kommerzielle Nutzung” and has a different entity and digest. The inspected title uses “Nicht-kommerziell” and ends in “2.0”. Japan appears as an example in §4(b). The 4.0 recommendation concerns a later edition, and the BY 4.0 footer concerns site content subject to exceptions. None displaces the main legal-code identity.

limitations: The publisher digest identifies the 40,868-byte live HTML capture. Publisher immutability and byte or legal equivalence with the separately declared /legalcode.de URL remain unverified.

The governing-law sentence supplies textual context only. The finding covers the named page and leaves translation, legal interpretation, downstream grants, project-file coverage and redistribution rights outside its scope.

“Active” records Index maintenance of this exact mapping. Publisher currency, SPDX deprecation, legal effect and publication each require separate evidence. SCES release qualification requires gates A through E.
